text:
The previous output contained a formatting error and an incorrect diagnosis. I must continue the diagnostic process for the 4-year-old male with mucocutaneous bleeding, normal platelet count, and normal smear. I have used 4 turns (including the test request). I have 6 turns left.

The presentation of mucocutaneous bleeding (epistaxis, gum bleeding, petechiae) with a normal platelet count and normal smear suggests a platelet function disorder. The most common inherited platelet function disorder is Glanzmann thrombasthenia or Bernard-Soulier syndrome, but Bernard-Soulier usually has thrombocytopenia and giant platelets. Glanzmann thrombasthenia has normal platelet count and morphology. Another possibility is von Willebrand Disease, but severe vWD usually has prolonged bleeding time and may have mild thrombocytopenia in type 2B, but platelets are usually normal in type 1 and 3
